draft.title: Discounts and mark-ups
card: A discount lowers a price. For a 20% discount, the new price is 100% − 20% = 80% of the old price, so multiply by 0.8.
A mark-up raises a price. For a 20% mark-up, the new price is 100% + 20% = 120% of the old price, so multiply by 1.2.
To find the multiplier, turn the percentage into a decimal. Subtract it from 1 for a discount. Add it to 1 for a mark-up.
Example: a $50 jacket with a 20% discount costs 50 × 0.8 = $40. A $50 item with a 20% mark-up sells for 50 × 1.2 = $60.
draft.remember: Discount: multiply by 1 minus the rate. Mark-up: multiply by 1 plus the rate.

a.q: Which multiplier gives the new price after a 15% discount?
a.why: A 15% discount leaves 100% − 15% = 85% of the price, so the multiplier is 0.85. The multiplier 1.15 is for a 15% mark-up, which raises the price instead.
a.clue: A discount takes the rate away from 1.

b.q: Sam buys mugs for $12 each and sells them with a 25% mark-up. What is the selling price of one mug?
b.why: A 25% mark-up means multiplying by 1.25, so 12 × 1.25 = $15. Adding only $0.25 mixes up the percentage with a dollar amount, which gives the wrong price.
b.clue: Add the rate to 1 to get the multiplier.
